candidate_theorem: On C4 tensor C4 let W=sum_(i!=j)d_ij[|ij>]+sum_i a_i[|ii>]-sum_(i<j)k_ij(|ii><jj|+|jj><ii|), with real coefficients and k_ij>=0. If W is nonnegative on every Schmidt-rank<=2 vector, then W=A+B^Gamma with A,B>=0. A common local diagonal phase gauge may be applied before stating the nonpositive real correlated offdiagonal condition. In arbitrary larger local dimensions the same conclusion holds when all offdiagonal correlated couplings occur among at most four aligned Schmidt-basis indices and all remaining terms are diagonal. This includes arbitrary sums of negative aligned projectors with phase-compatible nonnegative coefficients, not merely one rank-one subtraction. It does not classify correlated blocks with frustrated phases or general witnesses, and does NOT solve the unrestricted 4x4 PPT/SN3 problem. This is an UNREVIEWED WRITTEN CANDIDATE.
basis_and_basic_tests: 2-block positivity forces each a_i>=0 and d_ij>=0, by testing |ii> and |ij>. Put q_ij=sqrt(d_ij*d_ji). Testing x|ii>+y|jj> gives a_i*a_j>=k_ij^2. For each perfect matching M={ij,kl} and all z_i>=0, a rank-two matrix built as two rank-one 2x2 blocks with diagonal z_i,z_j and z_k,z_l yields f_M(z)=sum_i a_i*z_i^2-2*sum_(i<j)k_ij*z_i*z_j+2(q_ij*z_i*z_j+q_kl*z_k*z_l)>=0 after offdiagonal cost minimization; limits cover zeros. A real symmetric Z-matrix H (offdiagonals <=0) that is copositive is PSD, because x^T H x>=|x|^T H|x|>=0 for all real x.
graph_trichotomy: Draw the edge ij if q_ij<k_ij. A four-vertex graph is either disconnected, contains two disjoint edges forming a perfect matching, or is a spanning star: a connected graph without disjoint edges has pairwise-intersecting edges, hence is a star or triangle, and a triangle leaves one vertex isolated.
disconnected_case: Across components q_ij>=k_ij. If q_ij>0, take B_ij=(k_ij/q_ij)*[[d_ij,-q_ij],[-q_ij,d_ji]] on |ij>,|ji>; if q_ij=0 then k_ij=0 and set B_ij=0. These are PSD, their partial transposes cancel the cross-component correlated couplings, and all residual cross-pair diagonal terms are nonnegative. Each component restriction of W remains 2-block positive and has local dimension at most 3; it is PSD in dimension <=2 or decomposable in dimension 3 by the established Yang-Leung-Tang theorem https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.03534. Lift those decompositions and add the cross-pair PSD remainder and B^Gamma.
matching_case: For a perfect matching M of low edges, use B_ij=[[d_ij,-q_ij],[-q_ij,d_ji]] on each matching pair, PSD even when q_ij=0. The correlated block H of W-B^Gamma has diagonal a_i, matched offdiagonal q_ij-k_ij<0 and unmatched offdiagonal -k_ij<=0. For z>=0, z^T H z=f_M(z)>=0, so H is PSD by the Z-matrix fact. The remaining offdiagonal-basis diagonal terms are nonnegative; therefore W is decomposable.
star_setup: Let the low graph be a star with center 0 and leaves 1,2,3. Define t_i=k_0i>0 and b_i=t_i-q_0i in (0,t_i]; each leaf pair is high, so s_ij=q_ij-k_ij>=0. The two-index tests give a_0>0 and a_i>=t_i^2/a_0. Choose c_0i=q_0i and c_ij=min(q_ij,k_ij+b_i*b_j/a_0) on leaf pairs. For q_ij>0 define B_ij=(c_ij/q_ij)*[[d_ij,-q_ij],[-q_ij,d_ji]], and for q_ij=0 set B_ij=0. Then B=sum B_ij>=0 and A=W-B^Gamma has nonnegative offdiagonal-basis diagonal entries. Its correlated 4x4 block has center diagonal a_0, leaf diagonals a_i, center-leaf entries -b_i, and leaf-leaf entries min(s_ij,b_i*b_j/a_0). Its Schur complement in the center is the Z-matrix R with R_ii=r_i=a_i-b_i^2/a_0>=a_i-t_i^2/a_0>=0 and R_ij=-h_ij, h_ij=max(0,b_i*b_j/a_0-s_ij).
star_positivity: If every leaf pair has s_ij>t_i*t_j/a_0, all deficits h_ij vanish and R is PSD. Otherwise choose leaves j,k with s_jk<=t_j*t_k/a_0 and let i be the third leaf. For matching M={0i,jk}, substitute z_0=(b_i*z_i+t_j*z_j+t_k*z_k)/a_0>=0 in f_M(z)>=0. The resulting copositive leaf matrix C has diagonal C_ii=r_i, C_jj=a_j-t_j^2/a_0, C_kk=a_k-t_k^2/a_0 and offdiagonals C_ij=-k_ij-b_i*t_j/a_0, C_ik=-k_ik-b_i*t_k/a_0, C_jk=s_jk-t_j*t_k/a_0<=0. Each entry of R-C is nonnegative: diagonals use b_j<=t_j; i,j uses h_ij<=b_i*b_j/a_0<=b_i*t_j/a_0 and k_ij>=0; j,k follows by the two cases s_jk<=b_j*b_k/a_0 or >= that value, using b_j*b_k<=t_j*t_k and s_jk<=t_j*t_k/a_0. Hence R is copositive, and because R is a Z-matrix it is PSD. Its positive Schur complement gives A>=0, proving W=A+B^Gamma.

exact_example_check.observed: Exact Fraction arithmetic checks a 2-block-positive star example whose correlated negative matrix has rank 2, A and B are PSD of ranks 8 and 6, R and C are PSD, R-C is entrywise nonnegative, and a star deficit is 119/5020. W and W^Gamma are each non-PSD (test values -34/25 and -24/25). The example's 2-block positivity follows by adding a PSD rank-two-correlated perturbation to the previous trace-bound example. These finite checks do not establish the universal proof.
